morphblade is a turn-based strategy game developed and published by suspicious developments. morphblade stands out for it's minimalist design that still holds innovative gameplay mechanics. the grid-based game board is easy to navigate and clean vibrant colors distinguishing between different elements/symbols. the accompanying sounds effects/music enhance the overall experience, providing a fitting backdrop to the strategic gameplay. 

the core gameplay mechanic, and really the only gameplay mechanic revolves around placing and 'morphing' your game piece to eliminate waves of incoming enemies. there's a decent variety of enemy types and their distinct behavior adds depth to the gameplay, especially early when you first encounter new types. the turn-based nature of the game allows for thoughtful planning, and the limited number of actions per turn adds an extra layer of complexity.

morphblade features a well-paced learning curve, introducing players to new mechanics and enemy types gradually. the tutorial is effective in explaining the basic concepts, but mastering the intricacies of the morphing system requires time and practice. the game strikes a good balance between accessibility for casual players and depth for those seeking a more challenging experience.

morphblade offers a compelling blend of puzzle-solving and tactical decision-making. when paired with a minimalist game design, morphblade offers a unique and enjoyable experience no matter how much time you put into this. there's a sense of freshness while playing this, i have never played anything like it and i likely never will. i would suggest buying it at full price, but i cannot lie when i say that grabbing this on  massive discount makes it even more sweeter when you find out how fun it really is.

[b]morphblade[/b] is an endless/random grid- and turn-based tactical puzzler that offers hex and violence in spades.

you're the titular blade that morphs into all sorts of other things capable of killing giant bugs. or not, in which case they'll get pushed or you die. there are 6 tile types (plus blanks that can become anything) and they can be improved with 6 upgrades to be even more useful once enough bugs die on them. besides weapons there's teleport, repair, etc. and upgrades are stackable, so it's possible to create seriously overpowered hexes for some lovely ultraviolence against the waves of enemies. unless you keep pushing them off, in which case hexes don't get upgraded.

controls are mouse-only: left click to move, click on yourself to wait, tooltips for available tiles on mouseover, or right click on already active hexes and enemies for more info. these are all explained in-game in an amusing fashion, as expected from the developer of the excellent [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/206190/]gunpoint[/url]. as for hotkeys, esc opens/closes the menu, 'l' toggles the event log, arrows scroll it (and do nothing else). the log covers everything on the left, looks ugly, but also shows tile names and their levels, which should've been a separate toggle, I think.

settings only include a single volume slider (no music, so it's fine) and a windowed mode toggle for a resizable window. since presentation is as minimalistic as it gets, these are enough to satisfy basic needs.

it's a [b]basic but fun time-killer[/b], but with [b]only a single game mode without real goals or campaign[/b] or anything, it's gonna wear out its welcome sooner rather than later. [b]the 5 eur asking price is way too high, but might be worth it on sale[/b] if you're into this sort of thing.

An entertaining puzzle game that takes heavy inspiration from the board game "Hive" (a game I also recommend and can be found on here on Steam).

This is also a board game at heart; the action is turn-based, so logic and planning are the keys to victory. 

Like Hive, the board starts out with just a few spaces. The more rounds you play, the more spaces are added. Each type of space tile has its own special abilities which help you kill or evade enemies. These tiles can also be upgraded. Those upgrades will quickly become critical, as the easy enemy configurations early on gives way to some diabolical formations later on.

The game seems very simple at first, but this simplicity is deceptive. Within an hour of play, numerous new avenues of strategy become apparent, and adaptation becomes essential.

A fairly unique game that is a bit tricky to describe. 
I suppose it is a tactical, turn-based, combat-puzzler, area-control game.

You try to fight off waves of bugs who try to invade your area and attack you.  
The action you can perform depends on the tile you are standing on. You change into a different weapon (or tool) as you move onto each space, hence the name 'Morphblade'. 

As you progress, the enemies employ a variety of mechanics somewhat mirroring your own. At the same time, as you defeat enemies, your tiles get experience and upgrades. The possible upgrades depend on the adjacent tiles, each type of tile giving a unique option.

This therefore is a two-layer puzzle. There is a tactical layer as you try to survive any particular wave using your ever-changing movement and attack options on this turn-based hex-grid. But also a strategic layer as you try to organise and expand your tiles with a synergistic layout.

I really enjoy the mechanics of the game; I find them clever despite how simple they feel.
The sound and visual design is similarly very elegant.
